title.narrative: Better understanding of weather information and the use in Burundian agriculture

description.narrative: Reporting is an important management tool which is used to inform relevant government officials and other stakeholders about the results being achieved by individual projects and the programme as a whole. For project partners, it is compulsory to use the prescribed Orange Knowledge annual report format in order to report on project achievements. The annual report also provides valuable data on the financial situation of the project. Based on an analysis of the project performance in relation to the project output(s) and expected outcome(s), a revision of the project work plan may be suggested by the project partners. The consequences of a possible revision on the project work plan and budget must be made clear in the annual report. Nuffic monitors outputs and outcomes and not activities . Therefore, the main focus of the annual report must be on the achievement of the project’s output(s) and planned outcome(s). The information provided in the annual reports of the projects is used by Nuffic to monitor the progress of the project and to inform the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and other stakeholders about the output(s) and outcome(s) being achieved by individual projects and the Orange Knowledge programme as a whole. Please note that if project progress is in accordance with the original planning, reporting requirements are minimal. Only in case of deviations from the planning, more elaboration is demanded. In the grant award letter, the dates for submission of the annual reports are mentioned. In case of a three-year project, between 5-7 reports are obligatory. The first report (0) is a very short report which focuses on specific conditions and/or recommendations in the grant. There is no need to report on progress in achieving outputs and outcomes, which is done in the first annual report. As annex to the report 0, the consortium agreements between the partners should be submitted. The final report must reflect on the entire project period.

actual.value:
In total, Weather Impact provided 14 trainings to AUXFIN activators, distributed over two periods: November-December 2023 and February-March 2024. Ca. 800 activators operating in the 11 provinces of Burundi where AUXFIN Burundi is active – out of the country’s 18 provinces – participated in the training [Figure 2]. This involved key, master and super activators. All imparted trainings, as well as the training material, were bilingual – English and Kirundi. The trainings were live-translated into Kirundi. Most trainings were translated by Ms. Inès Irakoze, from AUXFIN Burundi. Others were translated by it was Mr. Mberincuti Andyman Wilson, that works as a freelancer translator.
Each training lasted two days. Both days were divided into two parts: The first half of the day comprised theory lessons and the second half, practical exercises on the use of AgriCoach. The first day covered meteorology basics, such as the definition of weather, meteorological processes such as rainfall, large-scale and small-scale weather, weather forecasts – how they are made and how they are presented on AgriCoach –, and how to interpret weather forecasts for agriculture. The second day covered the difference between weather and climate, seasonal forecasts – how they are produced and how they are represented on AgriCoach –, as well as how to use seasonal forecasts to support farming decisions. The content of the training was finetuned training after training, by carefully analyzing which explanations were understood better by the participants.
Theoretical classes were supported by slides with a high content of graphics and included frequent reception of questions from the participants. To transmit more complex concepts such as likelihood or the difference between weather and climate and between weather and seasonal forecasts, we utilized multiple-choice quizzes. Participants were handed a set of four colored cards where each color represented a different answer. In this way, they could select an answer by lifting the corresponding color card [Figure 3]. This exercise proved to increase participants’ engagement and also served as an effective energizer.
All practical exercises were group exercises and they were aimed at using and interpreting confidently all the features of AgriCoach. On the first day, participants had to analyze the weather forecast for the following day and perform a role play in teams of 3, in which one person adopted the role of a farmer, another person that of an activator, and the third person that of an assessor. The activator had to explain the weather forecast to the farmer, while the farmer had to ask the activator questions frequently posed by farmers in the G50s. The assessor had to observe the interaction, evaluate the capability of the activator to explain the weather forecast, reply to the farmers’ questions and lastly share their findings with the group. In the second day, participants had to use the crop selector to choose one crop based on their land type and obtain information about the crop. Then, they had to use the farming activity calendar to observe which activities were to be done at that time for the chosen crop. Finally, they had to use the seasonal forecast to evaluate whether said activities were advisable or whether they should recommend alternative to the G50 farmers.
For reference, the training slides and exercises are attached in Annex A of this report.
Due to the wide distribution of the activators across Burundi and the relatively large distances and challenging travel in Burundi, in almost all instances a team formed by the trainers from Weather Impact and support staff from AUXFIN Burundi travelled to each province, in order to ensure maximum participation. Only in two instances the training was done away from the province: for the activators from Bubanza, that received the training in the capital Bujumbura, and those from Cankuzo, who received it in Muyinga [Figure 2]. Table 1 shows all delivered trainings, with the dates attached, and the number of participants. While the trainings were planned to be received by 800 participants, only 774 attended, as can be seen in the table. The large discrepancies for Kayanza and Muyinga and Cankuzo combined is that in the initial plan, activators from Cankuzo would join the Kayanza training whereas at the end it was decided that they joined that in Muyinga.
Besides these trainings, on the 29th of November 2023 an introductory session with AUXFIN Burundi, the Geographic Institute of Burundi (IGEBU) and Weather Impact was held in Bujumbura as part of this project. IGEBU is a directorate general under the Ministry of Water, Environment, Land management and Urban Planning and is the national body responsible for, among others, meteorological monitoring and weather forecasting (i.e. the national meteorological agency). In this meeting, the three parties presented their activities and line of work with the intention to search for synergies and collaboration possibilities to maximize impact and reach as many smallholder farmers as possible with high quality weather and climate products. Office staff from AUXFIN Burundi were also present during this event, amounting to a total of 20 participants.
During and after the trainings, a set of training materials has been made available for activators on the UMVA platform. This includes: (1) training slides with complimentary text explanations and (2) 3 videos on i) the importance of weather information for agriculture, ii) an explanation of the 9-day weather forecast and iii) an explanation of the seasonal forecast, both provided on AgriCoach. The training slides are bilingual: English-Kirundi. The videos are in Kirundi. A version with English subtitles is available for reference on the following links:
• Video on the importance of weather information for agriculture: [https://youtu.be/wQkW2hqeJOM](https://youtu.be/wQkW2hqeJOM "https://youtu.be/wqkw2hqejom")
• Video on the 9-day weather forecast: https://youtu.be/TtPlApRiUdA
• Video on the seasonal forecast: [https://youtu.be/f6dnNF-Kpgs](https://youtu.be/f6dnNF-Kpgs "https://youtu.be/f6dnnf-kpgs")

comment.narrative: 03-07-2024: The trainings were given to AUXFIN Burundi (private), but also included 1 day training / high-level meeting with IGEBU (public), which is the national body in charge of delivering meteorological information. However it is important to note that this last component was a very minor part of the project.

title.narrative: B.I.6. Number of stimulating measures/extra facilities aimed at preparation, supervision and aftercare of female candidates

comment.narrative: 15-07-2024: Female activators were encouraged to join the trainings. There was a safe and respectful atmosphere in the trainings but one lesson learned is that it is extremely difficult for women with infants to join and effectively follow the trainings. In this context, one would think that child care could be a solution, but our local partners informed us on the unsuitability of such practice in the Burundian context. Therefore, this is a very difficult challenge that needs careful consideration if a true gender balance is to be targeted with such trainings.
